newsitem.title: CANADA: Simple majority not enough for separation - Chretien.
newsitem.headline: Simple majority not enough for separation - Chretien.

text.p: A simple majority vote in favor of Quebec separation would not be enough to trigger the province's secession from Canada, Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien said on Monday.

In an interview to be broadcast on the French cable news service of the Canadian Broadcasting Corp on Monday afternoon, Chretien said he would not recognize a result of 50 percent plus one vote for separation in a future Quebec referendum.
"Fifty percent plus one, in a third referendum, I find unreasonable," he said.

In the October 1995 referendum, Quebeckers voted 50.6 percent to 49.4 percent against sovereignty. Quebec separatists, including Premier Lucien Bouchard, have insisted that a simple majority vote in favor of sovereignty would be enough to begin the process of Quebec separation.
In the interview, Chretien said the threat of Quebec separation was the only obstacle to the recovery of Canada's economy.

The Liberal leader also criticized the advertising campaign and comments of Reform Party leader Preston Manning, which have suggested that voters should beware of voting for federal party leaders from Quebec.
Chretien said he did not think Reform would win more votes in Western Canada with an anti-Quebec ad campaign.
"I don't think there is an anti-Quebec sentiment," Chretien said.
